digest.component_or_area: dependency advisory detection and gating (pip-audit CI pipeline)
propositions: A committed lock freezes transitive dependencies, causing any published advisory against a pinned version to trigger build-stopping CI failures regardless of code changes.
Advisory failures punish unrelated authors when a capping dependency in an extra (e.g., inspect-ai capping click) produces a finding across multiple in-flight changes.
The pip-audit job's retry logic only handles DB-unreachable failures, making real findings non-recheckable and causing authors to repeatedly attempt `recheck` as their first response.

The gating must distinguish between Gerrit verify (block only when the change touches the dependency map) and scheduled main runs (block releases on known vulnerabilities), preventing unrelated changes from going red.
Overriding an advisory via `override-dependencies` requires evidence that the cap is stale, not real incompatibility, and must carry a REMOVE-WHEN condition to prevent permanent silent overrides.
A periodic canary job must notice when a dependency override's REMOVE-WHEN condition is met, following the established pattern of terraform-drift and prompt-eval scheduled checks.
